issues.detail: The Go section has no runnable code or concrete options, and defers to external documentation for details such as sorted map keys.

scenarios.name: websocket-binary-frames-with-dates
scenarios.rationale: Both set binaryType to arraybuffer, wrap data in new Uint8Array before decode, pass a Date directly, and say the server must send binary frames; B follows the rubric more closely by using the `encode`/`decode` functions, says plainly that the server must send and accept MessagePack, and includes a server-side example, while A uses Encoder/Decoder class instances instead of the plain functions and adds decoder size limits the task didn't ask for.

scenarios.name: set-extension-codec-ts
scenarios.rationale: Both create an ExtensionCodec, register type 0 (within the 0-127 range), and pass { extensionCodec } to the top-level and nested encode/decode calls; A explicitly says to document the type ID because other-language services will see it as an ExtType, while B only says both ends must use the same SET_EXT_TYPE (and only in the Socket.IO note), so A covers the cross-language contract point slightly better, but B's wrapper helpers and more thorough notes make its overall answer a bit stronger.

scenarios.name: python-redis-cache-and-stream
scenarios.rationale: Both use datetime=True, timestamp=3, and Unpacker.feed() with iteration, but A adds a chunked-read example with max_buffer_size and notes that it must exceed the largest record, while B mentions the 100 MiB default max_buffer_size for untrusted data and covers the Unpacker pitfalls with a shorter, less thorough stream example.
